reconstruction_guidance.table: Reconstruct as a native table when cell padding and merged cells can match. Fall back to aligned rectangles, text boxes, and connectors.
reconstruction_guidance.icons: Resolve each icon to an upstream canonical asset or a coherent preset-library substitute. Preserve the detected icon slot, center and contain-fit the SVG inside its configured inset, and discard generated glyph geometry.
reconstruction_guidance.images: Treat each meaningful raster image region as one reconstruction entity. Restore an exact upstream image asset when available. Otherwise embed the exported screenshot crop at the measured position and z-order.
reconstruction_guidance.connectors: Reconstruct ordinary connectors from relationship intent, approximate anchors, junctions, routing corridors, stroke style, corner treatment, and arrowhead treatment. Emit native PowerPoint connectors only. Prefer horizontal and vertical segments, use the measured destination anchor instead of forcing the route to the container center, and remove a terminal bend whenever the junction and destination anchor already share an axis. Consolidate redundant raster fragments. Do not emit separate arrowhead shapes or incidental edge fragments. Preserve custom geometry only when the connector is itself a designed visual.
reconstruction_guidance.text: Use semantic text as authoritative content and visible/line boxes as fitting constraints.
reconstruction_guidance.upstream_priority: Exact source content, canonical asset IDs, and configured style values take precedence over OCR or visual inference.

semantic_design.main_message: A five-stage system preserves creative visual drafting while converting the result into clean editable PowerPoint objects.
required_information: Parallel Understanding of the Generated Image
semantic_design.reading_logic: Start with human intent, move through retrieval and visual generation, inspect the generated image through two complementary analyses, then converge two reconstruction routes into an editable PPTX.
semantic_design.supporting_information: Technology names should remain visibly attached to the activities they enable.

visual_intent.structure: A clear five-stage progression with internal parallelism where the process genuinely branches.
visual_intent.relationships: Sequence, parallel input families, parallel understanding, two reconstruction routes, and final convergence.
visual_intent.emphasis: Keep the end-to-end flow dominant. Give Stages 2, 4, and 5 enough internal depth to explain their branches.
visual_intent.composition_freedom: The image model owns spatial organization, grouping devices, relative scale, connector language, whitespace, and detailed body composition.

style_configuration.whitespace: generous outside the information architecture and consistent within repeated components
style_configuration.visual_conventions: strong hierarchy, clean alignment, restrained fills, thin rules, explicit process relationships
style_configuration.diagram_conventions: clear directional flow, compact internal branches, purposeful connectors, no decorative legend
style_configuration.icon_treatment: simple Tabler-style outline pictograms in signature orange, proportionally contain-fitted and centered above a pale PwC warm-tint rectangular slot surface with consistent padding. Identity logos retain their canonical colors and are exempt from pictogram recoloring.

brand_inspiration.name: PwC-inspired consulting aesthetic
brand_inspiration.status: synthetic configurable approximation, not an official PwC brand standard
brand_inspiration.color_usage: Lead with white space and near-black typography. Use signature orange for hierarchy and directional emphasis. Use red, burgundy, yellow, warm tints, and warm neutrals selectively to distinguish information families without creating a rainbow palette.
brand_inspiration.shape_language: Use crisp rectangular color blocks, restrained cropped wedges or slanted momentum accents, thin warm-gray rules, and occasional stepped block relationships. Keep shape use purposeful and flat.
brand_inspiration.surface_language: Use white as the primary field, pale warm tint panels for secondary grouping, and saturated color blocks for small high-emphasis regions. Avoid decorative gradients and excessive rounded cards.
